lines.en: I pad softly through the bamboo.
My ringed tail keeps me balanced.
I hug the bamboo and climb.
My claws hook the bark and lift me.
I waddle over the fallen leaves.
I leap from stalk to stalk.
Short legs, but I keep pace.
My red fur flickers in bamboo shade.
I shuffle along a fallen log.
My paws crunch the dry leaves.
I steer around the thorny brush.
My tail swings past the rocks.
I creep sideways up the slope.
The bamboo tip sways under me.
I glance back, then move on.
I curl into a ball in the sun.
I lick my paws and wash my face.
I tuck my tail over my nose.
I doze with half-closed eyes.
I chew bamboo leaves slowly.
I prick my ears at the wind.
I sit on a branch and stare.
My whiskers twitch a little.
I scratch behind my ear.
I stretch my front legs out.
I yawn, showing small teeth.
I lick the fur on my chest.
I rest my chin on a log.
I shake off the fallen leaves.
I stare at the leaves, dazed.
I tip my little head at you.
I peek out from behind the bamboo.
My round eyes do not blink.
I stand up tall to look at you.
I lift a paw to test you.
My nose twitches, sniffing you.
You step close; I back half a step.
I lift my fluffy tail high.
My eyes are fixed on your hands.
I look down from my fork in the tree.

lines.zh: 我从竹枝上低头打量你
lines.en: I look you over from my bamboo branch.
I circle around your feet.
A soft rumble leaves my throat.
I blink to show I am not afraid.
My little head sways side to side.
I do not hide, I just watch.
You reach out; I sniff your fingers.
I slide down the bank to see you.
My wariness turns to curiosity.
I sit and wait for your move.
Ouch! My fur puffs up.
The blow rolls me into the bamboo.
Stop, I am hurt.
I curl up to guard my belly.
Blood reddens my front paw.
I cry out in pain.
That one really stung.
I drag my leg and retreat.
My ears flatten back.
I pant and lick the wound.
The smell of sweet berries!
I inch toward that berry.
The scent of bamboo pulls me in.
My nose is down, hunting the scent.
I stretch a paw to reach it.
Sweet berries, my favorite.
I rub your leg and beg.

lines.zh: 我盯着你手里那颗甜浆果
lines.en: I stare at the sweet berry in your hand.
I rise on tiptoe to sniff bamboo.
I cannot help one more step.
The sweetness makes me forget caution.
I hum softly against the bamboo.
Bamboo crackles in my mouth.
I hug the food and will not let go.
That smell keeps my feet moving.
I peek into your pockets.
I lick my lips for the next bite.
Bumped, I roll once.
Hey, that was my tail.
I bounce away, all fluff.
The hit shakes bamboo leaves off me.
I squeak and hop back.
We bump and tumble together.
I steady myself and look back.
My fur is squashed out of place.
The bump makes my paws slip.
I squeeze past between your legs.
I shake myself and stand up.
Pressed close, my fur is soft.
I bring her bamboo in my mouth.
We circle each other slowly.
Our tails touch, gentle.
I groom the fur behind her ears.
Our nest lies deep in the bamboo.
She leans in; I hold still.
We sit side by side chewing bamboo.
I call softly and she answers.
Together we line the nest with leaves.
Our wet noses touch.
I grab the berry and run.
I hug the bamboo with both paws.
I pop the found berry in my mouth.
I carry it back to the nest.
My paws bat at the little thing.
I catch a falling leaf in my teeth.
I stash the food under bamboo roots.
I gnaw it, juice on my face.
I lower my head and pick it up.
My mouth is full and I still stay.
Something moves; I look up.
I half rise and stare that way.
My tail stiffens; I am alert.
I catch the smell of a threat.
I block the way into the bamboo.
My claws dig into the branch.
A low growl builds in my throat.
I make myself look bigger.
Something nears my nest.
I get a clear look before I act.
I pace slowly around you.
My eyes stay locked on you.
I retreat behind the bamboo.
Each step is very light.

lines.zh: 我在竹林里等你先迈步
lines.en: I wait in the bamboo for your first step.
My tail sweeps the ground.
I watch you without a sound.
I press a front paw down.
I crouch, ready to spring.
When you move, I move.
I swipe with my claws.
I bite down on your sleeve.
I stand and slap at you.
I scratch, then pull back.
My small teeth clamp hard.
I lunge in from the side.
Two quick swipes, then I stop.
I pounce and bounce away.
I pin your foot with my paws.
One bite, then back to the bamboo.
The leaves stir; here I am.
I appear with two companions.
I slip out of the deep bamboo.
I arrive over fallen branches.
I sniff this ground first.
My red tail sweeps the leaves aside.
I drop from the tree to the ground.
Three red pandas crowd together.
I look up at this new place.
Paws down, I find my footing.
My fur is scorched and hot.
I fell from the bamboo.
Water floods my nose.
The blast knocks me over.
An arrow bites my shoulder.
Strange light numbs me all over.
Hunger has drained my strength.
Lightning stands my fur on end.
There is nothing under my paws.
